title: 1979 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Circles with centers \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) each have radius \(r,\) where \(1\lt r\lt2.\) The distance between each pair of centers is \(2.\) If \(B'\) is the point of intersection of circle \(A\) and circle \(C\) which is outside circle \(B,\) and if \(C'\) is the point of intersection of circle \(A\) and circle \(B\) which is outside circle \(C,\) then length \(B'C'\) equals

solutions.text:
Let \(A'\) be the analogous outer intersection of the circles centered at \(B\) and \(C.\) Then \(A'B'C'\) and \(ABC\) are concentric equilateral triangles. If \(K\) is their common centroid and \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} A'M&=\sqrt{r^2-1},\\ MK&=\frac{\sqrt3}{3},\\ AK&=\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}. \end{aligned} \] Similarity gives \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{B'C'}2&=\frac{A'K}{AK}\\ &=\frac{\sqrt{r^2-1}+\frac{\sqrt3}{3}} {\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}}. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(B'C'=1+\sqrt{3(r^2-1)}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Introduce the analogous point \(A'\) outside circle \(A\); symmetry makes \(A'B'C'\) equilateral
Use the common centroid and the altitude \(\sqrt{r^2-1}\) of an isosceles triangle with sides \(r,\) \(r,\) and \(2\)
